assets.scope: Mobile ooze family (ooze.lua); native occurrence spans the same 7-area pool as the jelly batch per docs/expansion-plan-20260928/PLAN.md; exact identity only, no subtype-wide substitution

references.note: Approved mobile amorphous-subject style anchor: reuse its steep overhead three-quarter camera, matte sculpted miniature finish, thin charcoal-brown physical disc and muted bronze-grey bevel, and how a low mobile organic mass leans toward one side of the disc to suggest a direction of travel. Do not copy its multiple discrete worm bodies or its colour.
Native black ooze colour only. Ignore the native flat blob rendering and its camera; our version is a sculpted three-dimensional mobile fluid.
Existing mapped white worm mass: its cluster of separate discrete grub bodies is already taken. Black ooze must read as one single continuous flowing fluid, never as multiple separate creatures.

prompt_fields.subject: One black ooze: a low, glossy, tar-black fluid mass leaning toward the lower-left with one thick blunt pseudopod extended in that direction, its surface pitted with small acid-eaten craters. A broad pale cool-grey rim-light highlight traces the leading edge of the pseudopod and the upper-left flank so the silhouette reads clearly against a dark disc.
prompt_fields.contrast: The other three oozes in this set are the same low mobile pseudopod body plan and must not be told apart by hue alone. Give black ooze the darkest overall value of the four, held readable only by a broad pale rim-light along its leading edge and pitted acid-crater texture across its glossy surface (silhouette: one thick blunt forward pseudopod with a pitted, uneven flank, distinct from yellow ooze's jagged angular tips, red ooze's rounded drips or blue ooze's faceted ice edges; value: near-black body carried entirely by a baked-in rim-light, not by a brighter faction ring).
prompt_fields.composition: One entire creature on one disc, steep overhead three-quarter view, its mass leaning toward one lower corner with one or two pseudopods extended in that direction to read as mid-crawl; the trailing edge stays lower and thinner. Every pseudopod stays inside the disc with the outer sixth of the disc radius left as bare base plate. Keep the leading pseudopod out of the upper-right rank corner and the upper-left interaction corner. No second creature, no trail residue outside the disc, no scenery.
prompt_fields.palette: Near-black tar with a cool dark undertone, small acid-etched pits across the surface, one broad pale silver-grey rim-light along the leading pseudopod and upper flank, deep black trailing shadow. No glow, no acid pool outside the body, no effect, no ground stain.
